languages._comment: Intake form section 1, اللغات: Dutch, Arabic, French. The section renders again (expertise page, plus a names-only row in the About ledger); it had been held as data only after being removed from display in an earlier build.
languages._comment_levels: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE LEVELS BELOW. The three languages are from intake section 1. THE PROFICIENCY LEVELS WERE NOT SUPPLIED AT INTAKE, THEY WERE INFERRED BY THE IMPLEMENTATION, and the English row is not on the intake form at all, it was added here too. Every such row carries status:'inferred', which is a third value alongside 'confirmed' and 'to-confirm' and exists so this is visible in the data itself rather than only in a commit message. The public page labels these rows via the expertise.levelInferred message key, so a visitor is told the levels are not self-reported. This CONTRADICTS intake section 8, 'Never assume a language level from the material supplied', one of only two MUST CONFIRM fields on the form. It was done at the client's explicit instruction after that conflict was put to them. THE CORRECT RESOLUTION IS TO ASK HER AND SET status:'confirmed' with her own answers, at which point the on-page caveat disappears by itself with no code change. Per-row basis for each inference is recorded in the `_basis` field, so a reviewer can audit them one at a time rather than as a block.
languages._comment_code_vs_locale: `code` NAMES THE LANGUAGE BEING DESCRIBED. The keys inside `name` are LOCALES, the language the label is written in. The Dutch row therefore reads code:'nl' and name.nl:'Nederlands', and the two 'nl' are a coincidence of the same tag meaning the same language in two different roles. Nothing in the code conflates them, localize() only ever reads `name` and `code` is only ever read as row.code, but a naive row[locale] lookup or a map over Object.keys(row) would, which is why this is written down.
